clue.text: Container that's dry inside trunk

indicators.note: inside says one thing sits within another, so the dry piece is placed within the trunk piece

parts.note: the bole is the trunk of a tree
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: A water flask kept dry inside a car boot or a travelling chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' suggests luggage or a car boot, but here it is the trunk of a tree; TT is short for teetotal, someone who stays dry.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottle is a glass or plastic vessel for holding liquids, an everyday kind of container.

clue.text: Key defenders with speed

parts.note: backs are defensive players in football and rugby
pace is speed, as of a runner

explanation.surface: A football coach saying the crucial thing is fast defenders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like an adjective meaning crucial, but it is a key on a keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Backspace is the keyboard key that deletes the character before the cursor.

clue.text: Explosive musical beat, in short, endlessly excellent thing

indicators.note: in places the explosive, musical and beat pieces within the shortened word
without an end means the word for short loses its final letter

parts.note: terse means short or curt in speech
HE stands for high explosive
Cats is the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical
to whisk is to beat eggs or cream

explanation.surface: A rave review of a show with an explosive, catchy beat.
explanation.walkthrough: The commas break the clue so that 'in short' looks like the phrase meaning briefly; 'short' is really a word for curt, and 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The cat's whiskers is an old idiom for something or someone outstanding, the very best.

clue.text: Advanced tips for ideal pulse

parts.note: advanced money is money lent

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its two ends, so only its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Hints on getting an ideal heart rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' looks like a heartbeat, but it is the food: pulses are edible seeds such as beans, peas and lentils.
explanation.definitionFit: A lentil is a small edible legume seed, one example of a pulse.

clue.text: Pathetic pieces of work that aren't even engraved

indicators.note: pieces that are not even are the odd-numbered ones, so only the first and third letters stay

parts.note: the odd-numbered letters, first and third, of the word work
to etch is to engrave a design into metal or glass

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on shoddy craftwork, not even properly engraved.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces of 'work' that are not in even positions are its odd letters, W and R; add ETCHED for WRETCHED.
explanation.definitionFit: Wretched and pathetic both describe something miserable, pitiful or of very poor quality.

clue.text: One with oar in crew originally raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters are read upwards, so bottom to top
in says the answer is sitting within the run of letters of the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A boat crew member who first raised an oar.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside cREW ORiginally lies REWOR; 'raised' in a down clue sends it upwards to read ROWER. 'Originally' looks like a first-letter signal but is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower is a person who propels a boat with oars, so someone holding an oar in a crew.

clue.text: Fight to keep Rhode Island in shape

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the fight word holds the state abbreviation within it

parts.note: a tangle is a fight or scuffle
RI is the postal abbreviation for the US state

explanation.surface: A scrap to keep the state of Rhode Island in good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In shape' reads as an idiom for fit, but 'shape' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangle is a geometric figure with three sides and three angles, an example of a shape.

clue.text: Real faith in cool, fantastic song

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful and wild, so the letters before it are rearranged into a fresh order

parts.note: all fifteen letters used as fodder

explanation.surface: Praise for a great track about keeping faith and staying calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fantastic' looks like praise for the song, but it signals the rearrangement of the four words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotel California is the 1977 title track of the Eagles album, one of the best-known rock songs.

clue.text: Fear start of difficult study

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
to read a subject is to study it at university

explanation.surface: A student's anxiety at beginning a hard course.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great fear or apprehension about something to come, so it matches fear as a noun.

clue.text: Reform of laws, sane, ethical and immaculate

indicators.note: to reform something is to form it again, so the letters that follow are put into a new shape

parts.note: all fifteen letters used as fodder

explanation.surface: A campaigner's plea for legal reform that is sensible, ethical and beyond reproach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reform' reads as political change to legislation, but it tells you to rework the letters of the three words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean as a whistle is an idiom for spotless, without any stain or wrongdoing, just like immaculate.

clue.text: Stripped of power, explain betrayal

indicators.note: stripped of means deprived of, so the abbreviation is taken away from the word for explain

parts.note: to spell out is to explain in detail
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: An ousted leader demanding a full account of the treachery.
explanation.walkthrough: SPELL OUT without its P gives SELL-OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sell-out is a betrayal of principles or allies, usually for money or personal gain.

clue.text: Length of time that is left for dog

parts.note: a span is a stretch or period of time
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone working out how long they have to leave something for the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaniel is a breed of gun dog with long drooping ears, an example of a dog.

clue.text: Offensive and motivated, caused continuing annoyance

parts.note: rank means foul-smelling or offensive
to be led is to be moved or driven to act

explanation.surface: Some behaviour, offensive and deliberate, that left a lingering grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offensive' looks like a description of the definition, but it is the first building piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rankled kept irritating a person long afterwards, a lasting sense of resentment or bitterness.

clue.text: Further from initial source

indicators.note: from says the answer is drawn out of the letters of the words that follow it

parts.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Going further back, right to the original source of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside initiAL SOurce. 'Further' looks like a verb or a distance word, but it is the adverb meaning in addition.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and further both serve as adverbs adding another point: moreover, in addition, as well.

clue.text: Adviser working with sovereign in court

indicators.note: in places the working and sovereign pieces within the abbreviation for court

parts.note: CT is the usual abbreviation for court
a machine that is on is working
a sultan is a Muslim sovereign ruler

explanation.surface: A royal adviser busy with the king at the palace court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like the royal setting of the scene, but it only supplies its two-letter abbreviation as the outer shell.
explanation.definitionFit: A consultant is a professional paid to give expert advice, so an adviser by trade.

clue.text: Farewell so full of purpose, very loud

indicators.note: a thing full of another holds it, so the purpose word sits within the first word

parts.note: taken as written
an end is an aim or purpose
ff, fortissimo, is the musical direction for very loud

explanation.surface: A goodbye that is deliberate and extremely noisy.
explanation.walkthrough: ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud, a direction found in printed scores.
explanation.definitionFit: A send-off is a gathering or demonstration of goodwill for someone leaving, a farewell occasion.

clue.text: Brief rest at inn, refreshed

indicators.note: refreshed means made new again, so the letters of the preceding words are reworked

parts.note: the nine letters used as fodder

explanation.surface: A short stop at a pub that leaves the traveller refreshed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refreshed' sounds like the traveller after a drink, but it tells you to rework the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Transient and brief both mean lasting only a short while, passing quickly.

clue.text: Man apprehending sneer changed sweater

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters of the scornful word are put in another order
apprehending means arresting and holding, so the man word grips the other letters within it

parts.note: a guy is a man
the five letters reworked

explanation.surface: A man arrests a sneering suspect who then changes his jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweater' could be someone who sweats; it is the knitted garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A guernsey is a thick knitted woollen jumper, originally worn by fishermen of the Channel Islands.

clue.text: Tiring, getting cross, engaged in treatment of huge stain

indicators.note: treatment means processing or working over, so the following letters are reworked
engaged in means involved within, so the cross letter goes inside the reworked letters

parts.note: the nine letters reworked
a cross is written as the letter X

explanation.surface: Someone worn out and irritable while scrubbing at an enormous stain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an angry mood, but it is X, placed inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhausting work is tiring work: both adjectives describe something that drains energy and wears a person out.

clue.text: Prima donna eager to return

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word for eager is read from end to start

parts.note: avid means keen or eager

explanation.surface: An opera star impatient to come back to the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated leading female opera singer, which is exactly what prima donna names.

clue.text: Hostile article on part of Bible

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
the Bible is divided into chapters and verses

explanation.surface: A hostile newspaper article about a passage of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts A above VERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Averse means strongly opposed or disinclined, close to hostile in 'averse to change'.

clue.text: Wind spool finally after film by artist

parts.note: a film of mist is a thin haze covering something
RA, Royal Academician, is a standard crossword artist

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word before it, keeping only its last letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Instructions for winding a reel of film by a filmmaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' reads as a verb about winding a spool, but it is the noun. 'After' puts L at the end; 'film' is a thin coating, not a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: The mistral is a strong, cold northerly wind that blows down the Rhône valley into southern France.

clue.text: Plan ends in special care for tree

parts.note: a map is a plan or chart

indicators.note: the ends of the next words are their last letters, so only those are taken

parts.note: the final letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A gardener's plan to give a tree particular attention.
explanation.definitionFit: The maple is a broad-leaved tree known for its lobed leaves and sweet sap, one kind of tree.

clue.text: Appearance from rising sun receiving approval

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the approval word is put within the turned word
in a down clue, rising means the word goes upwards, so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun
OK signals approval

explanation.surface: A sunrise view that wins approval for its beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: SOL reads upwards as LOS, which then holds OK.
explanation.definitionFit: Looks means outward appearance, as in judging someone by their good looks.

clue.text: Plain old vehicle occupied by six officers initially

indicators.note: a vehicle occupied by passengers holds them, so the six and officer pieces go within it

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a bus is a road vehicle
VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the word before it is used

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: An ancient army truck carrying half a dozen officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' could be a noun for flat land, but here it is the adjective meaning clear; O for old comes from abbreviations such as OE for Old English.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain here means clear and evident to anyone, which is what obvious means.

clue.text: Meeting for journalists with bias covering extremes of serious fraud

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the bias word encloses the other pieces

parts.note: a preference is a leaning or bias towards one thing

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outermost letters, the first and the last

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
a con is a swindle or fraud

explanation.surface: Reporters gathering about a biased cover-up of a serious fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: The inserted letters split the bias word after its third letter, leaving the -FERENCE ending intact as the second word of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A press conference is an event where a spokesperson briefs reporters and answers their questions.

clue.text: Influence is held by established writer

indicators.note: a thing held by another is gripped within it, so the first two pieces sit inside the abbreviation

parts.note: est. is the abbreviation for established
to have a say is to have influence
taken as written

explanation.surface: An established author's sway over others.
explanation.walkthrough: Est. is the abbreviation seen on shop signs and labels, as in 'est. 1850', meaning established in that year.
explanation.definitionFit: An essayist is an author of essays, a particular kind of writer of short prose pieces.

clue.text: Go quiet during precious time

indicators.note: during means in the course of, so the quiet letter falls within the precious word

parts.note: dear means precious or beloved
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Advice to leave silently at a cherished moment.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes inside DEAR, then T follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart is to leave or set off, the same sense as go in 'we must go now'.
